notes: Reader/Writer/Seeker are std::io::Read/Write/Seek and the composite interfaces are trait bounds. Go's io.EOF is Ok(0) from Read (std convention) and an io::Error carrying rust_stdlib::io::Error::Eof elsewhere (rust_stdlib::io::eof, is_eof); the other error variables are the variants of rust_stdlib::io::Error (Error::is is errors.Is). Go's (n, err) results are Result values whose error carries the count: CopyError::written for Copy/CopyBuffer/CopyN and ReadError::read for ReadFull/ReadAtLeast/ReadAt. Copy/CopyBuffer/CopyN (kept for Go's partial count and ErrShortWrite) do not dispatch to WriterTo/ReaderFrom nor shrink the buffer for a LimitedReader; CopyBuffer with an empty buffer is an error where Go panics; a negative Go count for CopyN is zero. ReaderAt/WriterAt keep Go's contract (the buffer is filled unless an error, io.EOF included, says why not) with u64 offsets like std's FileExt; an offset above i64::MAX is Go's negative offset. MultiWriter does not flatten or forward optional interfaces; a Read that returns Ok(0) for a non-empty buffer is EOF (so ErrNoProgress is produced only by repeated Interrupted); dropping a pipe half does not close it, as in Go. Pipe halves are cloneable handles; PipeWriter::write_shared reports the bytes consumed before an error and PipeReader::read_raw is Read with Go's exact result, including Ok(0) for a zero-length write. Tested against Go by tools/io_check.py.

ByteReader.note: `Read::bytes` yields one byte at a time; bufio::Reader::read_byte is the buffered, unreadable form.

ByteScanner.note: std has no unread; bufio::Reader and text::Reader/Buffer provide read_byte/unread_byte.

Closer.note: Rust closes on drop; types with an explicit, fallible close have an inherent `close` (os::File, PipeReader, PipeWriter).

Copy.note: Does not dispatch to WriterTo/ReaderFrom nor shrink the buffer for a LimitedReader, as Go does.

CopyBuffer.note: Does not dispatch to WriterTo/ReaderFrom; an empty buffer is an error where Go panics.

CopyN.note: Does not dispatch to WriterTo/ReaderFrom, as Go's Copy underneath does; a negative Go count is zero.

Discard.note: std::io::Sink discards writes; Go's Discard also has ReadFrom/WriteString fast paths, which only affect performance.

LimitReader.note: Take stops with EOF after n bytes; a negative Go n is take(0).

MultiReader.note: Chain two readers at a time; fold for more. Behaviour matches Go's MultiReader for conforming readers.

MultiWriter.note: Does not flatten nested MultiWriters or forward optional interfaces such as StringWriter.

NopCloser.note: A reader needs no Close in Rust: use it as is.

OffsetWriter.Seek.note: Seeking from the end is an error, as in Go.

PipeReader.Read.note: read_raw is Go's exact Read, including Ok(0) when a read consumes a zero-length write; the std::io::Read impl skips such writes because Ok(0) means EOF to std.

PipeWriter.Write.note: write_shared writes through a shared handle and reports the bytes consumed before an error; the std::io::Write impl is the same without the count.

ReadCloser.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read` and an explicit close or drop.

ReadSeekCloser.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read + Seek`; close by drop.

ReadSeeker.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read + Seek`.

ReadWriteCloser.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read + Write` and an explicit close or drop.

ReadWriteSeeker.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read + Write + Seek`.

ReadWriter.note: No named trait: use the bound `Read + Write`.

ReaderFrom.note: `copy(&mut dst, &mut src)`; types with a faster path have an inherent read_from (os::File, bufio::Writer, text::Buffer).

WriteCloser.note: No named trait: use the bound `Write` and an explicit close or drop.

WriteSeeker.note: No named trait: use the bound `Write + Seek`.

WriterTo.note: `copy(&mut src, &mut dst)`; types with a faster path have an inherent write_to (os::File, bufio::Reader, text::Reader).
